answer: Ephemeral Quill Signing Levy: each identity must attach a freshly generated quill signature to every outbound message, priced by a ferrous-weighted fee curve that rises with message volume and decays only after a fixed quiet period. A lantern audit trail logs signature reuse; duplicates trigger escalating surcharges. An attacker running N sock puppets pays O(N²) in fees per epoch, since each identity's curve resets independently but volume compounds across the fleet. Honest low-volume agents stay near zero cost.
